chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Anbasa, the freedman of al-Rashid, narrated to us, he said: Darim ibn Qubaysa narrated to us, he said: Na'im ibn Salim narrated to us, he said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) say:

On the Day of Ghadeer Khumm, while he was holding the hand of Ali (peace be upon him): Do I not have more authority over the believers than they have over themselves? They said: Yes. He said: Hence, whoever I am his Mawla, then this is Ali his Mawla. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be enemy to whoever opposes him, and support whoever supports him, and abandon whoever abandons him.

key_terms.أَوْلَى: More worthy or having more authority
key_terms.غَدِيرِ خَمٍّ: Ghadeer Khumm, the location where the event took place

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's declaration 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa Aliyun mawlahu' at Ghadeer Khumm?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of *Wilayah* through the Prophet's public affirmation of Ali's authority at Ghadeer Khumm. The term 'Mawla' is interpreted by Shia scholars as denoting comprehensive leadership and spiritual succession, reinforced by the Prophet's immediate supplication for divine support of Ali's partisans and opposition to his adversaries.
